For a **typical single electric blanket**, I’d look at a power station with about **1,000 Wh of capacity**. A good option is the **[BLUETTI AC180](https://dealectric.com/go/bluetti-ac180)**: it has a 1,152 Wh battery and 1,800 W AC output, and one guide estimates it can run a 120 V blanket through the night. [Dealectric’s comparison](https://dealectric.com/power-station-to-run-a-heated-blanket-all-night)

Runtime depends a lot on the blanket’s wattage and heat setting. A 1,024 Wh station may run an approximately 100 W blanket for around eight hours, but a higher-draw queen blanket could need substantially more capacity. [Tested Watts](https://testedwatts.com/2026/09/24/power-station-electric-blanket/) estimates about 2,600 Wh for eight hours at 260 W. Check the blanket’s label, and plug it directly into the station—keep the station off the bed.
